title: Ἵππος καὶ ὄνος
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 141. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ἄνθρωπός τις εἶχεν ἵππον καὶ ὄνον.
sentences.tr: Anthrōpos tis eichen hippon kai onon.
sentences.l: A certain man had a horse and a donkey.

sentences.t: Ὁδευόντων δέ, ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ εἶπεν ὁ ὄνος τῷ ἵππῳ· « Ἆρον ἐκ τοῦ ἐμοῦ βάρους, εἰ θέλεις εἶναί με σῶν. »
sentences.tr: Hodeuontōn de, en tēi hodōi eipen ho onos tōi hippōi· « Aron ek tou emou barous, ei theleis einai me sōn. »
sentences.l: And as they were travelling, on the road the donkey said to the horse: « Take some of my load, if you wish me to be safe. »
sentences.n: Ὁδευόντων δέ is a genitive absolute whose subject is left unexpressed — "with them travelling", the two animals understood from the line before. ἆρον is the aorist imperative of αἴρω, "lift, take up"; ἐκ with the genitive is partitive here, "some of". σῶν is the accusative of σῶς, "safe and whole", contracted from the older σάος.

sentences.t: Ὁ δὲ οὐκ ἐπείσθη· ὁ δὲ ὄνος πεσὼν ἐκ τοῦ κόπου ἐτελεύτησε.
sentences.tr: Ho de ouk epeisthē· ho de onos pesōn ek tou kopou eteleutēse.
sentences.l: But he was not persuaded; and the donkey, having fallen from the toil, died.
sentences.i: But the horse would not be persuaded; and the donkey dropped under the strain and died.
sentences.n: ἐπείσθη is the aorist passive of πείθω: Greek says "he was not persuaded" where English says "he refused". ἐκ τοῦ κόπου is cause, "out of the labour". Chambry's ano teleia (·) marks a stop lighter than a full stop and heavier than a comma.

sentences.t: Τοῦ δὲ δεσπότου πάντα ἐπιθέντος αὐτῷ καὶ αὐτὴν τὴν τοῦ ὄνου δοράν, θρηνῶν ὁ ἵππος ἐβόα· « Οἴμοι τῷ παναθλίῳ, τί μοι συνέβη τῷ ταλαιπώρῳ ;
sentences.tr: Tou de despotou panta epithentos autōi kai autēn tēn tou onou doran, thrēnōn ho hippos eboa· « Oimoi tōi panathliōi, ti moi synebē tōi talaipōrōi ;
sentences.l: And the master having put everything upon him, and the donkey's very hide as well, the horse, lamenting, cried out: « Alas for me, all-wretched that I am — what has befallen me, poor sufferer?
sentences.i: And when the master had loaded everything onto him, the donkey's hide into the bargain, the horse wailed aloud in lament: « Alas for me, wretch that I am — what has come upon me in my misery?
sentences.n: Another genitive absolute. αὐτὴν τὴν … δοράν: αὐτός in this position is "the very…" — the skin itself went up on top of the load, so that the horse now carries the donkey twice over. οἴμοι takes a dative of the person bewailed, here the speaker himself. Chambry sets a space before the Greek question mark; the speech runs on into the next line, so the » is still open.

sentences.t: μὴ θελήσας γὰρ μικρὸν βάρος λαβεῖν, ἰδοῦ ἅπαντα βαστάζω, καὶ τὸ δέρμα. »
sentences.tr: mē thelēsas gar mikron baros labein, idou hapanta bastazō, kai to derma. »
sentences.l: for, not having been willing to take a small burden, look, I carry everything, and the hide too. »
sentences.i: for because I would not take up a little of the load, see now — I carry it all, hide and all. »
sentences.n: μὴ θελήσας, an aorist participle with μή rather than οὐ, gives the reason and the condition at once: "because I refused". βαστάζω is to carry a weight, to hold it up. Chambry prints ἰδοῦ with a circumflex where the usual accent is ἰδού; the page is followed as it stands.

sentences.t: Ὁ μῦθος δηλοῖ ὅτι τοῖς μικροῖς οἱ μεγάλοι συγκοινωνοῦντες οἱ ἀμφότεροι σωθήσονται ἐν βίῳ.
sentences.tr: Ho mythos dēloi hoti tois mikrois hoi megaloi synkoinōnountes hoi amphoteroi sōthēsontai en biōi.
sentences.l: The fable shows that the great, sharing with the small, both of them will be kept safe in life.
sentences.i: The fable shows that when the great make common cause with the small, both come safe through life.
sentences.n: συγκοινωνέω takes the dative of the party one shares with. The sentence is loosely built: οἱ μεγάλοι … συγκοινωνοῦντες is taken up again by οἱ ἀμφότεροι, "both of them", a resumption classical prose would not need. σωθήσονται is future passive of σῴζω, "will be kept safe".
